ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: Even with unique IDs, `Allocation` has no structural validation for its indicator matrix. At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L699) the dataclass accepts any `matrix`, but the readers at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L716), [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L725), and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L734) assume shape `(len(task_ids), len(model_ids))` and binary entries. I verified that `Allocation(task_ids=['t1'], model_ids=['m1'], matrix=np.array([[1,0],[0,1]]))` is accepted and then silently drops the extra row/column: `get_assigned_models('t1')` and `get_assigned_tasks('m1')` both report only the first logical slot. Because accessors also test `== 1`, non-binary entries would be misread rather than rejected. This is distinct from the already-found duplicate-ID problem: a structurally malformed matrix can corrupt audit/load semantics even when identifiers are unique.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `Allocation.__post_init__()` validation that enforces `matrix.shape == (len(task_ids), len(model_ids))` and that all entries are binary `{0,1}`. Fail fast on mismatch instead of letting accessors silently ignore extra rows/columns or misread non-binary values.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_NEW12  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: The probabilistic feasibility API is stateless and therefore unsafe for incremental dispatch to a model that already has committed load. `LoadBalancer.feasibility_probability()` and `dispatch_check()` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1020) only compare the passed `task_load` against `model.L`; `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3534) forwards the same scalar with no notion of existing assigned tokens. I verified that with `L=100`, two successive checks of `80` then `40` both return feasible, even though the cumulative committed load would be `120`. In other words, the helper can answer “does this standalone prompt fit?” but cannot answer the Area-2 question “does this next dispatch keep the model within capacity?”  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the API to accept `projected_total_load` or `(current_load, additional_load)` and make callers pass cumulative committed load, not just the next prompt size. If the intention is truly “total load,” rename the parameter accordingly and enforce it at the manager boundary.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_LB_R2_NEW13  
SEVERITY: 0.62  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: Cross-component, verified from this scope: the dispatch false-positive monitor has a write path for blocks but no wired write path for later success recovery. `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` records blocks at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3550), and `DetectorHealthMonitor.check_dispatch_health()` explicitly looks for “blocked earlier, succeeded later” evidence at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2672). But the only success recorder, `record_dispatch_success_after_block()`, exists at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4180) and has no call sites in the manager, orchestrator, or tests. That means the pathology can only ever see the “blocked” half unless external code remembers manual bookkeeping, so the health monitor under-detects the very false positives it was added to diagnose.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Wire `record_dispatch_success_after_block()` into the standard successful decomposed-dispatch path, or introduce a single manager-owned dispatch result hook that records both block and later success transitions automatically.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

These were the strongest new findings I could verify after filtering out issues already covered in earlier rounds.
